title: Interruption-safe rollout playbook (experiment orchestration)
body:
Purpose and scope

Quick notes: this is a working playbook to run cross-functional experiments and rollouts that are resilient to mid-exposure interruptions (capacity spikes, regional outage, model degradation). Focus is on choreography, cheap synthetic probes, human-in-the-loop decision windows, and fail-open vs fail-closed choices.

Target audience: product owners running feature rollouts that touch the Redwood Runtime, SRE/oncall, solutions eng (customer-facing staging), and console/observability engineers.

High-level goals
- Keep user-visible disruption minimal during interruptions.
- Ensure fast, safe rollback or diversion with minimal blast radius.
- Provide clear decision signals (both automated and human) so stewards can act confidently.
- Limit cost/regression exposure during experiments.

Definitions (short)
- Interruption: any unexpected event during a progressive exposure window that materially affects SLOs (latency, error volume), model quality (regression, hallucination), or cost (token burn). Examples: GPU pool degradation, model cache thrash, sudden token cost spike.
- Steward: primary person responsible for the progressive rollout window (usually product or solutions engineer).
- Conductor: SRE or runtime engineer who can execute traffic switches/fallbacks.

Pre-flight checklist (before any canary or A/B exposure)
- [ ] Confirm steward + conductor names on the ticket and Slack thread.
- [ ] Create a single rollout thread: #rollouts + pinned doc (link).
- [ ] Canary slice definition agreed (user cohort, geography, synthetic sampler).
- [ ] Baseline metrics (last 7d): p50/p90/p99 latency, error rate, token/call median cost, hallucination proxy (top-k OOVs or eval-set BLEU/accuracy), human-reported NPS if applicable.
- [ ] Synthetic probe harness staged (PR: serving-runtime/pull/1287) with stress traffic and golden prompts.
- [ ] Circuit breaker thresholds configured in Console for the experiment route.
- [ ] Rollback activation window defined (timeboxed human decision window).

Traffic partitioning pattern recommended
1) Synthetic-only (0% real traffic) — smoke + stress probes for 30–60m.
2) Microcanary (0.1–0.5% of eligible traffic) — short-lived, watch p50/p95/p99 + hallucination probe for 1–3 hours.
3) Microstep expansion (0.5% -> 2% -> 5%) every 1–2 hours with automated checks.
4) Pause points with human judgement after each step for higher-risk features.

Decision signals (automated gating)
- Latency: p99 increase > 2x baseline OR absolute p99 > 1500ms triggers pause.
- Errors: 5xx increase > 3x baseline or absolute > 0.5% triggers pause.
- Cost: per-call token spend > +40% over baseline for two consecutive windows triggers review.
- Quality: evaluation harness degradation > 5% (relative) on golden prompts OR hallucination proxy spike triggers pause.
- Downstream user signals: increased human support tickets with samples flagged as severity 2+ triggers immediate escalation.

Operational patterns for interruptions
Scenario A — capacity drop in primary cluster during stage 2 expansion
- Automated: route policy should already fallback to a lower-cost model variant or region if available. If not, circuit breaker reduces canary traffic to last healthy slice.
- Steward action: convene conductor + SRE, evaluate synthetic probe logs and GPU metrics.
- Escalation: if capacity projection indicates >30m recovery time, revert canary to previous routing (rollforward is dangerous).

Scenario B — sudden quality regression (model output quality measured by evals)
- Automated: flag raised in Optimize QA dashboard; experiment paused automatically.
- Human: steward reviews first 200 failing golden prompts, samples the live user samples. If regression persists, trigger immediate rollback and create an incident ticket (INFRA-4123 style).

Scenario C — price spike/cost anomaly
- If cost anomaly ephemeral (<30m) and low impact, throttle exposure automatically.
- If sustained, stop expansion and notify finance/growth leads. Consider fallbacks like lower-quantized model variant or caching.

Runbook for a mid-exposure interruption (step-by-step)
- 0m: Alarm triggers (Console signal or SLO pager).
- 0–2m: Conductor acknowledges pager, posts to #rollouts with link to the thread and the experiment id.
- 2–5m: Automated mitigation kicks: traffic diverted to safe fallback config, canary weight reduced to 0.5x.
- 5–10m: Steward and conductor assess probe output, check synthetic harness results, collect first 100 user request IDs for sampling.
- 10–20m: If root cause not quickly remediable, either (a) pause expansion and keep microcanary at reduced weight for monitoring, or (b) re-route all canary traffic to baseline model. Decide based on predicted user impact and recovery ETA.
- 20–60m: Post-decision: notify stakeholders, create incident ticket if rollback chosen, run a targeted retrospective within 48h.

Roles & responsibilities (quick)
- Steward (product/solutions): owns hypothesis, monitors quality signals, calls rollback.
- Conductor (SRE/runtime): executes traffic switch, has runbook access to orchestration.
- Observability owner (console): tunes and surfaces signals in dedicated experiment dashboard.
- Support lead: triages user tickets and surfaces user-facing examples.

Human-in-the-loop ceremony (recommended)
- For all expansions above 5% exposure, require a 15-minute decision window where the steward summarizes: 1) current metrics vs baseline, 2) synthetic probe pass/fail, 3) proposed next weight and rollback plan.
- Record the decision in the rollout thread with a timestamp and a short rationale.

Lightweight postmortem template (if interruption caused rollback)
- What happened (1–2 lines)
- Timeline of key events (timestamps)
- Root cause hypothesis
- Why automated signals did/didn't catch this
- Actions: short (<7d) and medium (<30d)
- Owner(s) for each action

Practical heuristics and gotchas (notes to self)
- Synthetic probes are cheap but brittle — rotate prompts weekly and keep a small golden-set for regression triage.
- Don’t conflate latency noise in cold-start windows with real degradations — look at sustained windows and KV cache hit ratios.
- Be explicit about cost gating thresholds in the ticket; surprises lead to slow decision-making.
- For multi-model orchestration: prefer deterministic fallback mapping (model A -> model A-quantized) to avoid semantic drift during fallback.

Short TODOs (next actions)
- [ ] Add an automated telemetric summary card to the experiment dashboard: delta vs baseline for the 5 signals above. (Owner: Rhea)
- [ ] Build a quick Slack bot that can reduce canary weight to X% on command and log the event (Owner: Samir).
- [ ] Draft a customer-facing explanation template for rollbacks (Owner: Arjun).

Open questions
- What is an acceptable hallucination proxy threshold for top-line consumer features? (need product input)
- Do we prefer immediate full rollback vs stepping down to a lower-fidelity model during quality regressions? This impacts user experience and cost — tradeoffs doc needed.
- How to automate detection of semantic drift for non-deterministic generation workloads?

Useful links and references
- Linear ticket sample: INFRA-4123 (capacity fallback work)
- PR: serving-runtime/pull/1287 (canary routing helper)
- Console runbook template (Confluence)
- Slack channels: #rollouts, #oncall, #console-observability

Notes: this is intentionally a compact working document. Will expand into a full playbook and a companion Slack automation script. Keep this in the solutions eng repo under docs/rollouts as a living draft.

-- Maya (wip)
